add.title: Add environment
add.body: Name it now, or let the first agent name it after its host.

name.label: Name (optional)
name.helper: Leave this empty to use the host's name when the first agent connects. You can rename it later.

rotate.title: Show install command
rotate.description: Generate a new join token and its install command.
rotate.alert: This replaces the previous token. Install commands you copied earlier stop working. Agents that are already enrolled aren't affected.

step2.title: Install the agent
step2.body: Run one of these on a swarm manager or on a standalone host. Coaming detects which it is.

helper.swarm: Run it on any manager node. It creates a Docker secret for the join token and starts the agent as a global service, so nodes you add later enrol by themselves.
helper.standalone: Run it on the host. It starts the agent container with the Docker socket mounted.
helper.composeSwarm: Save this as `coaming-agent.yml` and run `docker stack deploy -c coaming-agent.yml coaming-agent`.
helper.composeSwarmSecret: Create the secret first with the command in the file's first line.
helper.composeStandalone: Save this as `coaming-agent.yml` and run `docker compose -f coaming-agent.yml up -d`.

update.heading: Update the join token on this swarm
update.helper: Docker secrets can't be edited, so this command removes the old secret and adds the new one.
update.serviceName: It is for an agent installed with the command, whose service is named `coaming-agent`. If you installed from the stack file, the service is named after your stack, such as `coaming-agent_coaming-agent`; change the name in the command to match.

install.secretNotice: This command contains a secret. It starts with a space so shells that ignore space-prefixed commands keep it out of history. Once your hosts are enrolled, rotate the token from Settings.

errors.create: Couldn't create the environment. Try again, and check the Coaming logs if it keeps happening.
errors.rotate: Couldn't generate a new token. Try again, and check the Coaming logs if it keeps happening.

publicUrlRequired.before: Coaming doesn't know what address to give the agent. Set the public URL or the agent URL in

insecureAgentUrl.before: Agents can't connect to this Coaming: the address they'd dial is plain ws:// for another host, and agents refuse it. Set an https public URL or agent URL in
insecureAgentUrl.after: , then try again. COAMING_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE=true on Coaming allows a plain address for development only.

waiting.heading: Waiting for the first agent…
waiting.body: This updates by itself when the agent connects.
waiting.slow: Still waiting? Check that the host can reach {{url}}, then look at the agent's log: `docker logs coaming-agent` (standalone) or `docker service logs coaming-agent` (swarm).
waiting.detected_one: Detected a {{kind}} with {{count}} node. Opening it now…
waiting.detected_other: Detected a {{kind}} with {{count}} nodes. Opening it now…
